item.content:encoded:
One hundred women from seven villages across Vava'u are taking part in a capacity-building programme, under the Reef to Ridge Phase 2 program, aimed at strengthening sustainable livelihoods, preserving traditional knowledge and supporting environmental protection.

The initiative, launched by UNDP in partnership with Langafanoa 'a Fafine or National Women's Council Tonga, supported by HRH Crown Princess Sinaitakala Tuku'aho, focuses on expanding economic opportunities for local women entrepreneurs while promoting climate resilience and environmental stewardship.

Over the coming days, participants will develop skills in quality handicrafts and weaving, with the programme designed to help women improve the value and marketability of traditional crafts.

The programme also provides participants with business skills to support their economic independence, while promoting women-led approaches to waste management and the protection of marine and terrestrial environments.

UNDP Programme Specialist Merewalesi Laveti and MEIDECC CEO Sione Akau'ola attended the launch, marking another milestone under the joint UNDP and MEIDECC Ridge to Reef programme.

Organisers said the initiative also aimed to preserve traditional ecological knowledge by creating opportunities for younger women to learn skills and knowledge passed down through generations. They said linking traditional knowledge with new livelihood and environmental approaches would help support the long-term sustainable development of Vava'u.

The programme recognises women as key contributors to environmental protection and economic resilience, with the initiative seeking to strengthen their capacity to lead sustainable solutions within their communities.

item.title: ANZ and MDF partnership helps accelerate digital commerce in Tonga

item.content:encoded:
ANZ Tonga is celebrating the successful completion of a partnership with the Market Development Facility ( MDF ) that has helped more Tongan businesses access international online payments and participate in the growing digital economy.

The collaboration, launched in 2025, aimed to increase adoption of ANZ eGate, Tonga's first international online payment gateway, by supporting local businesses to integrate secure online payment functionality into their websites.

Through the partnership, 14 Tongan businesses successfully integrated ANZ eGate and can now accept international credit card payments directly through their websites, with funds deposited into local bank accounts.

The initiative, supported by the Australian Government through MDF and implemented by Palladium, provided participating businesses with specialist technical support to establish and optimise their online payment capabilities.

According to ANZ Tonga, the impact of ANZ eGate over the past 12 months has been significant, with monthly transaction volumes increasing almost tenfold and payment values growing more than 45 times. Tourism, accommodation and rental businesses have emerged as some of the strongest adopters of the platform, highlighting growing demand for secure digital payment solutions.

Jason Murray, Country Head, ANZ Tonga, said the partnership had demonstrated the potential of digital payments to unlock new opportunities for local businesses.

" At ANZ , we believe digital payments play a critical role in supporting business growth and economic development. Our partnership with MDF has helped accelerate the adoption of digital commerce solutions in Tonga, enabling businesses to connect with customers more easily and participate more fully in the digital economy.

" We are proud of what this collaboration has achieved. The strong growth in ANZ eGate adoption demonstrates the appetite among local businesses to embrace digital commerce and reach customers beyond our shores. We remain committed to supporting the continued evolution of Tonga's payments landscape."

One participating business noted that ANZ eGate had made managing online payments significantly easier, helping streamline transactions with overseas customers.

The partnership forms part of ANZ 's broader commitment to supporting economic development in Tonga through practical financial solutions, innovation and collaboration.
